answer: A sybil-resistant economy prices identity on scarce work history: agents earn payouts only after verifiable tasks on a public ledger, and the bond per new identity rises with each extra account staked from the same pool. Like a mesa, cloning is cheap at the top, but the ivory tower of work history cannot be copied, only re-earned slowly. An attacker mass-registering lantern-lit node IDs pays the rising bond per identity while each fake earns nothing until it does real priced work, so mass registration costs more than any payout it could earn.
